look_here_first: Native Texas annual; inspect mature green elongated narrow spikelets with several florets. Lemma bodies are commonly 9–12 mm, with an awn around 6–10 mm and slightly 2-toothed tip; measure glume, lemma, and awn to rule out introduced Japanese and lanceolate bromes. Flowering yellow anthers can be visible, but are NOT species-specific.

best_field_traits: Annual (not perennial) native Texas brome of open woodland/grassland sites.
Sheaths with soft recurved/retrorse hairs; blades often ~3–7 mm wide.
Fertile lemmas typically ~9–12 mm, with a two-toothed apex and one 6–10 mm awn.
Spikelets multi-flowered, borne on branching panicle.
Fertilizing yellow anthers may be conspicuous at flowering, but are common to other grass taxa.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Fresh whole plant plus annual crown and habitat
Two mature spikelets with actual mm ruler
Fertile lemma showing two terminal teeth and 6–10 mm awn
Hairy sheath and real ligule collar
crew_field_check: LOOK AT THE SPIKELET, NOT JUST THE DROOP: all four bromes have several florets stacked along one spikelet, often with lemma awns. First decide ANNUAL vs PERENNIAL, then count florets, measure the entire spikelet, individual lemma and awn, and inspect the glume veins and leaf sheath hairs. Nodding inflorescences or long awns alone are not a species ID.
Measure actual mature spikelet(s) with a millimeter ruler.
Inspect lemma/glume or true ligule ONLY where detailed pixels or a collected macro are actually available.
Record uncertain grass to genus, don't force the species from one photo.

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. japonicus is an introduced annual with often smaller 10–15 mm spikelets, longer awns and more flexuous nodding branches. B. lanceolatus has often much larger many-flowered spikelets and longer lemmas. B. pubescens is a perennial of moist shady woods with broader leaves. All split characters require scale: green, slender spikelets alone are not enough for native vs introduced labels.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: Annual japonicus / lanceolatus / texensis versus perennial woodland pubescens. Small loose kinked heads japonicus; giant lance-shaped spikelets lanceolatus; damp shaded perennial pubescens; Texas annual texensis demands short-awn/lemma comparison.
